cls: Centrally acting antihypertensive - alpha-2 adrenergic agonist
quick: Initial 0.1 mg orally twice daily (morning and bedtime); usual 0.2-0.6 mg/day in divided doses
May be taken with or without food; larger portion at bedtime eases dry mouth/drowsiness
Crosses the placenta; use only if clearly needed. Do not stop abruptly
Excreted in human milk; use with caution in nursing women
Lower initial dose may be needed; monitor closely. No supplemental dose after hemodialysis
About 50% metabolized in liver; use with caution
Blood pressure and heart rate; do NOT stop abruptly - taper to avoid rebound hypertension
summary: Clonidine is a centrally acting alpha-2 adrenergic agonist used to treat hypertension, alone or with other agents. By stimulating brainstem alpha-2 receptors it reduces sympathetic outflow, lowering peripheral resistance, heart rate, and blood pressure within 30-60 minutes of an oral dose. Its most clinically critical hazard is rebound hypertension on abrupt discontinuation - the dose must always be tapered. Common dose-related effects are dry mouth, drowsiness, dizziness, sedation, and constipation.
indications: Treatment of hypertension (alone or with other antihypertensive agents)

dosage.n: Elderly patients may benefit from a lower initial dose

dosage.d: Increase by 0.1 mg/day at weekly intervals until desired response
dosage.n: Taking the larger portion at bedtime minimizes dry mouth and drowsiness

dosage.d: Lower initial dose; titrate to response with careful monitoring
dosage.n: Only minimal clonidine removed by hemodialysis - no supplemental dose needed

admin: Do not stop abruptly - taper the dose gradually over 2 to 4 days to avoid rebound hypertension and withdrawal symptoms
If discontinuing in a patient on a concurrent beta-blocker, withdraw the beta-blocker several days before gradually stopping clonidine
Take the larger portion of the daily dose at bedtime to reduce daytime dry mouth and drowsiness
Continue therapy to within 4 hours of surgery and resume as soon as possible afterward, monitoring BP
Adjust dose to the individual blood pressure response
moa: Clonidine stimulates alpha-2 adrenoreceptors in the brainstem, reducing sympathetic outflow from the CNS. This decreases peripheral and renal vascular resistance, heart rate, and blood pressure, with reductions in plasma renin activity and catecholamine/aldosterone excretion. Normal postural reflexes are largely preserved, so orthostatic symptoms tend to be mild.

relative: Sinus node dysfunction or AV block (sympatholytic action may worsen conduction)
Concurrent sympatholytic drugs (risk of severe bradycardia)
Cerebrovascular or coronary insufficiency (caution with BP swings)
monitor: Blood pressure (including for rebound on withdrawal)
Heart rate / for bradycardia and AV block

preg: Clonidine crosses the placental barrier. No adequate, well-controlled studies in pregnant women exist; animal data show increased resorptions at some doses. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed, and do not discontinue abruptly.
lact: Clonidine is excreted in human milk; exercise caution when administering to a nursing woman.
renal: Patients with renal impairment may benefit from a lower initial dose and require careful monitoring. Elimination half-life is prolonged (up to ~41 hours in severe impairment). Only a minimal amount is removed by routine hemodialysis, so no supplemental dose is needed after dialysis.
hepatic: About 50% of an absorbed dose is metabolized in the liver. Use with caution in hepatic impairment.

major: Beta-blockers - worsen rebound hypertension on withdrawal; can potentiate bradycardia/AV block (withdraw beta-blocker first when stopping clonidine)
Agents affecting sinus/AV node (digitalis, calcium channel blockers, beta-blockers) - severe bradycardia; sinus bradycardia requiring pacemaker reported with diltiazem or verapamil
moderate: Tricyclic antidepressants - reduce the hypotensive effect of clonidine (may need dose increase)
Neuroleptics - may induce or worsen orthostatic regulation disturbances
CNS depressants (barbiturates, other sedating drugs) - additive depressant effects
minor: High IV haloperidol - theoretical increased arrhythmogenic potential (relevance to oral clonidine not established)
interactions.food: Food does not influence clonidine pharmacokinetics
interactions.alcohol: Avoid - clonidine potentiates the CNS-depressant effects of alcohol
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor heart rate with sinus/AV-node-affecting drugs; weakly positive Coombs' test reported

serious: Rebound hypertension on abrupt discontinuation - do not stop abruptly; taper to avoid (rare hypertensive encephalopathy, CVA, and death reported)
Bradycardia, sinus node arrest, high-degree AV block, arrhythmias
emergency: Severe rebound hypertension / hypertensive crisis after abrupt withdrawal - urgent care; reversible with oral clonidine or IV phentolamine
Severe bradycardia requiring IV atropine/isoproterenol or temporary pacing

monitoring: Blood pressure (and titrate to response); do not stop abruptly - taper to avoid rebound hypertension
Heart rate for bradycardia and AV conduction, especially with other sympatholytics
Blood pressure perioperatively (continue to within 4 h of surgery)
counsel: Do not stop this medication abruptly - taper under your clinician's guidance to avoid rebound hypertension (a dangerous rise in blood pressure, headache, nervousness, tremor)
Do not interrupt therapy without your physician's advice; refill on time so you never run out
May cause drowsiness, dizziness, and sedation - use caution driving or operating machinery
Avoid alcohol and other sedating drugs, which increase the sedative effect
Dry mouth and constipation are common; taking the larger portion of the dose at bedtime can help
Contact-lens wearers may notice dry eyes
pk: Blood pressure declines within 30-60 minutes of an oral dose
Peak plasma levels in ~1-3 hours; maximum BP decrease at 2-4 hours
Elimination half-life ~12-16 hours (up to ~41 hours in severe renal impairment)
Sustained over the dosing interval; given in divided doses (typically twice daily)
Store at 25 C (77 F), excursions 15-30 C; dispense in a tight, light-resistant container
pearls: Do not stop abruptly - taper to avoid rebound hypertension; risk is greater after higher doses or with concurrent beta-blockers
When stopping a patient on both clonidine and a beta-blocker, withdraw the beta-blocker first, then taper clonidine
Oral bioavailability is high (70-80%); pharmacokinetics are dose-proportional from 100-600 mcg
No therapeutic effect in hypertension due to pheochromocytoma
Children with vomiting illnesses are especially prone to rebound hypertension from missed doses
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered. If it is nearly time for the next dose, skip the missed one and resume the regular schedule - do not double up. Do not skip doses or stop the drug on your own, as missing doses can cause blood pressure to rebound.
overdose: Overdose may cause early hypertension followed by hypotension, bradycardia, respiratory depression, hypothermia, drowsiness, diminished/absent reflexes, weakness, irritability, and miosis; large overdoses can cause cardiac conduction defects, apnea, seizures, and coma. CNS depression may be more frequent in children (as little as 0.1 mg has caused toxicity). There is no specific antidote; care is supportive (atropine for bradycardia, fluids/vasopressors for hypotension, vasodilators for hypertension; naloxone may help respiratory depression). Dialysis is not effective.
